F01.question: I området Recursive self-improvement, vad är de två senaste nyheterna och vad handlar de om?
F01.answer:
The two most recent papers about Recursive self-improvement (RSI) with feed dates of 2026-09-16 are:

[30] ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents, which introduces a paradigm that couples harness evolution with model reinforcement learning. It creates an "inner recursion" that improves the harness while keeping the model fixed, and an "outer recursion" that trains the model under the improved harness. This approach transforms researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into tasks for continual learning, enabling scientific AI to evolve alongside the research it supports [30].

[31] ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement, which proposes a framework that contrasts successful and failed trajectories for the same task and aggregates evidence across tasks to identify recurring behavioral deficiencies. It decomposes the evolvable harness into five functional modules (Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection) that evolve independently within a restricted modification scope before being integrated into a unified harness [31].

F02.question: Vad har hänt med GUI agents den senaste månaden?
F02.answer:
Based on the provided sources, several significant developments have occurred with GUI agents in the past month:

A new benchmark called GUI-Primitives was introduced to diagnose spatial reasoning failures in vision-language GUI grounding, featuring 994 contrastive instruction pairs over seven spatial relations in graphical user interfaces [26]. This addresses a critical gap in evaluating how well agents understand spatial relationships within UIs.

The AnTrap benchmark was developed to systematically evaluate GUI agents' robustness against runtime anomalies, revealing that even top models suffer significant performance degradation when encountering dynamic issues like unexpected pop-ups [27].

MobilePA-Bench was presented as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating mobile planning agents, featuring 13 functional domains and 212 realistic mobile tools, with evaluation across dimensions like sub-agent collaboration and memory usage [25].

UI-Mate was introduced as a foundation GUI agent that integrates an environment-grounded training stack with in-context demonstration learning, setting a new open-weight state of the art on general computer-use benchmarks with 77.0% on OSWorld-Verified [29].

LLaDA-UI was developed as a block-wise diffusion vision-language GUI agent that outperforms existing models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B on multiple GUI benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of diffusion models for latency-sensitive GUI applications [28].

UI-Venus-2 was introduced as a general-purpose foundation GUI agent designed to operate across mobile, web, and desktop environments through a unified closed-loop reasoning-action framework, expanding environment coverage to over 170 multilingual mobile apps and native desktop operating systems [30].

EASEL was proposed as a benchmark evaluating dexterous visual tool use in multimodal agents, which is a critical capability for fine-grained visual action in GUI environments [23].

TRACE was introduced to address the memory and latency challenges GUI agents face when accumulating high-resolution screenshots during trajectories, using trajectory-robust admission with evidence ordering [21].

F03.question: Vad är det absolut  senaste inom Video genereation och är det hårdvaru- eller mjukvarurelaterat?
F03.answer:
The absolute latest in video generation as of the most recent sources is PhysStream [31], which was published on 2026-09-16. PhysStream is a software-based framework for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis that incorporates structured scene memory (positional maps and object tracking maps derived online) and supports fine-grained motion control through sparse velocity-increment signals. It's designed for interactive, mid-generation control over multi-object tabletop rigid-body scenes, improving physical consistency by reducing motion distribution distance (FVMD) by 33% and trajectory error by 12% over baseline methods.

PhysStream is clearly software-related rather than hardware-related, as it describes a model architecture with specific technical components like bidirectional model finetuning and causal autoregressive training [31]. The framework focuses on improving the quality and controllability of generated videos through algorithmic innovations rather than hardware advancements.

The next most recent video generation work is LynnReal-Omni [29], which also describes a software framework for native multimodal video generation that achieves faster inference (377 ms for 22-frame 540p video on a single H100 GPU), but PhysStream is the absolute latest with a 2026-09-16 publication date [31].

Among these, Benchmark Radar [25] is the most recent source (2026-09-14) that provides an overview of the current landscape of coding agent benchmarking, while Real Suite [20] represents a newer benchmark that has been introduced to address saturation in existing coding benchmarks.

F07.question: Vad säger forskningen om text-to-video den senaste månaden?
F07.answer:
The research on text-to-video in the last month includes two key studies:

[22] Introduces Temporal Context Routing (TCR), which maps script timing onto the shared temporal axis of video and audio generation, improving alignment between text prompts and video content. TCR reduces Shot Boundary MAE by 96% (from 1.11s to 0.042s) and raises Dialogue Accuracy by 55.8 percentage points (from 28.3% to 84.1%) compared to baseline models [22].

[29] Presents FIRM-Video, a framework for reliable text-to-video reward modeling that uses a "check-before-score" principle. It constructs dimension-specific checklists, verifies each criterion against temporal visual evidence, and aggregates only verified decisions to improve evaluation accuracy and reduce unfaithful justification in text-to-video model assessment [29].

Additionally, there is a news report about MiniMax's new video model that can generate a 15-second video in 13 seconds, demonstrating text-to-video generation speed improvements, though this is a product announcement rather than research [25].

F11.question: Vad hände i forskningen förra veckan?
F11.answer:
This week's research included several significant developments across AI research. ModularRSI introduced a new framework for generalizable harness evolution in recursive self-improvement, decomposing agent harnesses into five functional modules for improved transferability [1]. MetroLLM-Bench presented a 955-case benchmark for testing language models as transit kiosk runtimes, covering six metro systems and eleven categories including routing and accessibility [4].

Researchers developed ReactHuman, the first physics-grounded benchmark for human-like reactive decision-making in embodied multimodal LLMs, testing models on 1,000+ scenes with exact ground truth from rigid-body simulation [5]. E2A-Bench was introduced to evaluate evidence-to-action reliability in financial chart reasoning, revealing three hidden failures in existing hallucination evaluations [7].

Emergence World created a continuously running multi-agent environment for adversarial stress testing of long-horizon autonomous systems, demonstrating that individually capable agents can form systems with qualitatively different failure modes [8]. Lightning Weave improved the accuracy-efficiency frontier of reasoning models through capability composition, raising HMMT 2025 accuracy from 59.2% to 64.0% with 10.7% fewer response tokens [13].

Drift-Constrained Optimization established a new approach to fine-tuning instruct models by constraining behavioral drift, with results showing substantial improvements in scientific reasoning and multilingual translation [19]. ScienceBuddy was released as an interactive scientific research workspace that brings continually improving scientific agents into researchers' everyday workflows through recursive-in-recursive self-improvement [26].

OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, which is described as "the best model available" and "the most capable and powerful model you can use right now" [2]. The model is being positioned as a significant step in AI capabilities, with claims that it "just destroys all the other models" [20].

GPT-6 Astra is described as capable of running autonomous workflows, building software factories, and handling complex tasks without constant human intervention [12]. One user reportedly "left it alone for five days" with "tens of thousands of emails, years of writing, calendar contacts" and Astra "built Ethan a personal knowledge system" [28].

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is being marketed as a step toward AGI (Artificial General Intelligence), though there's skepticism about this claim. The sources note that "AI still really sucks at determining when something is AI" - a capability that would be expected if AGI had been achieved [25].

OpenAI is developing a "work" system that allows ChatGPT to carry out tasks on supported websites and continue working after the computer is closed [27]. This system supports "applications inside the conversation" and "a cloud browser that can carry out tasks on supported websites and keep on working after you close your computer" [27].

OpenAI has a product called "GPT finance," which "combines GPT6 Astra with financial data sets and tools for producing actual banking research" [15].

Some sources mention OpenAI's claim about the "AGI era" and note that "Jensen Huang, the CEO of NVIDIA, said yesterday he declared that we have AGI because of Astra" [12], though the sources express skepticism about this claim.

F15.question: Vad har hänt med AI-agenter den senaste veckan, i både papers och videor?
F15.answer:
This week has seen several significant developments in AI agents across both papers and videos:

New agent frameworks and capabilities:
- Researchers introduced "HazardAuditor" to make computer-use agents safer, addressing safety risks that emerge through runtime behavior rather than just generated content [7].
- "RSIAgent" enables autonomous exploration for recursive self-improvement in new environments, allowing agents to adapt without retraining [18].
- "Agent as Policy" (AGP) demonstrates that general-purpose agents can directly drive physical robots without task-specific training, achieving success rates of 100% on some manipulation tasks [11].
- "Atria Dawn Preview" is a foundation agentic language model designed for scientific research, with humans and AI collaborating as "project-level partners" rather than just task-level executors [22].

Agent applications and tools:
- "Claude Code" has become a popular skill that drives computer use across applications, with the creator documenting failure modes and building a full workflow for agents [9].
- "AI software factories" powered by GPT-6 Astra are being developed to let agents build applications autonomously, with the creator showing how to set up a 24/7 system for building applications [4].
- Agents are starting to make purchases on behalf of users, with Stripe building systems to handle agent payments for things like buying coffee [28].

Agent evolution and business integration:
- "Occamy-1.0" presents a cost-efficient co-work model that remains competitive with larger frontier systems while focusing on practical agent capabilities [3].
- The concept of "AI second brains" is evolving into "team brains" that extend productivity to collaboration, with creators reporting saving about 20 hours per week [19].
- "Gavel" (from "The Router Within" paper) enables skill routing in frozen LLMs, outperforming retrieval pipelines that add up to 16B external parameters [2].

Safety and trust developments:
- "Emergence World" provides adversarial stress-testing for long-horizon multi-agent systems, revealing that individually capable agents can form systems with new failure modes [25].
- Companies like Stripe are building systems to handle agent payments, with the creator noting they "would trust AI to buy me coffee" but not yet to "sign up for a subscription" [28].
